edition.description: Continuous chapter numbering 1–61 (Volume I: 1–23, II: 24–42, III: 43–61).

characters.name: Elizabeth Bennet
characters.summary: Second of the five Bennet daughters: quick-witted, lively, and her father’s favourite.

notes.text: Overhears Mr. Darcy call her merely “tolerable” at the Meryton assembly and resolves to dislike him.
Refuses Mr. Darcy’s first proposal.
Rereading Darcy’s letter, realises she has misjudged both Darcy and Wickham.
Accepts Darcy’s second proposal.

characters.name: Jane Bennet
characters.summary: Eldest Bennet daughter: beautiful, gentle and inclined to think well of everyone.

notes.text: In London, Caroline Bingley’s coldness shows her the friendship was insincere.
Becomes engaged to Mr. Bingley.

characters.name: Mr. Bennet
characters.summary: Sardonic, bookish gentleman of Longbourn whose estate is entailed away from his daughters.

characters.name: Mrs. Bennet
characters.summary: Excitable, nervous mother whose great object in life is marrying off her daughters.

characters.name: Mary Bennet
characters.summary: Third Bennet sister: studious, moralising and eager to display her accomplishments.

characters.name: Kitty Bennet
characters.summary: Fourth Bennet sister, fretful and easily led by Lydia.

notes.text: Improves greatly once removed from Lydia’s influence and spends more time with her elder sisters.

characters.name: Lydia Bennet
characters.summary: Youngest Bennet sister, fifteen: bold, flirtatious and wild about the militia officers.

notes.text: Goes to Brighton as the guest of Colonel Forster’s young wife.
Elopes with Wickham.
Returns to Longbourn married, and lets slip that Darcy was at her wedding.

characters.name: Charles Bingley
characters.summary: Amiable, wealthy young man who takes the lease of Netherfield Park.

notes.text: Leaves Netherfield for London, apparently not intending to return.
Proposes to Jane and is accepted.

characters.name: Caroline Bingley
characters.summary: Bingley’s elegant, proud younger sister.

notes.text: Writes to Jane that the party will not return and hints that Bingley may marry Georgiana Darcy.

characters.name: Louisa Hurst
characters.summary: Bingley’s elder, married sister.

characters.name: Mr. Hurst
characters.summary: Louisa’s indolent husband, who lives to eat, drink and play cards.

characters.name: Fitzwilliam Darcy
characters.summary: Wealthy, reserved master of Pemberley in Derbyshire; Bingley’s closest friend, thought proud and disagreeable by Meryton.

notes.text: Privately begins to admire Elizabeth’s “fine eyes”.
Proposes to Elizabeth and is refused.
His letter explains his conduct towards Wickham and his part in separating Bingley from Jane.
Is revealed to have found Lydia and Wickham and secretly paid for their marriage.
Proposes again and is accepted.

characters.name: Georgiana Darcy
characters.summary: Darcy’s much younger sister, an accomplished musician.

notes.text: Darcy’s letter reveals that Wickham persuaded her, at fifteen, to agree to an elopement.
Meets Elizabeth and proves painfully shy rather than proud.

characters.name: Lady Catherine de Bourgh
characters.summary: Domineering, aristocratic patroness of Mr. Collins, mistress of Rosings Park.

notes.text: Descends on Longbourn to forbid Elizabeth to marry Darcy.

characters.name: Anne de Bourgh
characters.summary: Lady Catherine’s sickly, silent daughter and heiress.

characters.name: Colonel Fitzwilliam
characters.summary: Darcy’s gentlemanly cousin, younger son of an earl.

notes.text: Unwittingly tells Elizabeth that Darcy saved a friend from an imprudent marriage.

characters.name: Mrs. Reynolds
characters.summary: Long-serving housekeeper at Pemberley.

characters.name: George Wickham
characters.summary: Handsome, charming new officer in the militia regiment quartered at Meryton.

notes.text: Tells Elizabeth that Darcy cheated him of a church living promised by Darcy’s father.
Darcy’s letter exposes his dissipation and his attempted elopement with Georgiana.
Runs off with Lydia Bennet.
Has his debts paid and a commission bought by Darcy on condition he marry Lydia.

characters.name: Mr. Collins
characters.summary: Pompous clergyman, Mr. Bennet’s cousin and heir to the entailed Longbourn estate.

notes.text: Proposes to Elizabeth and refuses to believe her refusal.
Becomes engaged to Charlotte Lucas within days.

characters.name: Charlotte Lucas
characters.summary: Elizabeth’s sensible, practical friend, twenty-seven and unmarried.

notes.text: Accepts Mr. Collins for the security of a comfortable home.

characters.name: Sir William Lucas
characters.summary: Charlotte’s genial father, knighted while mayor and fond of recalling his presentation at St James’s.

characters.name: Mr. Gardiner
characters.summary: Mrs. Bennet’s sensible, gentlemanly brother, a London merchant.

notes.text: Takes public credit for settling Lydia’s marriage, though Darcy paid.

characters.name: Mrs. Gardiner
characters.summary: Mr. Gardiner’s intelligent, elegant wife and a favourite with her elder nieces.

notes.text: Warns Elizabeth against encouraging Wickham.
Her letter tells Elizabeth the truth of Darcy’s part in Lydia’s marriage.

characters.name: Mrs. Phillips
characters.summary: Mrs. Bennet’s sister, married to a Meryton attorney.

phases.label: Married
phases.note: An ill-matched marriage of long standing.

phases.label: Father & daughter
phases.note: She is his favourite.

phases.label: Mother & daughter
phases.note: Her mother’s favourite.

phases.label: Sisters
phases.note: Kitty follows wherever Lydia leads.

phases.label: Aunt & niece
phases.note: A trusted confidante.

phases.label: Cousins
phases.note: Collins will inherit Longbourn under the entail.

phases.label: Cousins
phases.note: Lady Catherine intends them to marry and unite the two estates.

phases.label: Mutual dislike
phases.note: He slights her at the assembly; she laughs at him.

phases.label: Sparring
phases.note: He begins to admire her; she remains convinced he is proud and disagreeable.

phases.label: Rejected proposal
phases.note: Elizabeth refuses him, citing Jane and Wickham.

phases.label: Thawing
phases.note: At Pemberley his altered manners surprise her.

phases.label: Separated
phases.note: Bingley leaves for London; his sisters and Darcy discourage the match.

phases.label: Eloped
phases.note: They leave Brighton together without marrying.

phases.label: Flirtation
phases.note: She is charmed by him and readily believes his story.

phases.label: Disillusioned
phases.note: Darcy’s letter overturns her opinion of him.

phases.label: Rejected proposal
phases.note: She refuses him firmly; he assumes it is modesty.

phases.label: Engaged
phases.note: A marriage of prudence rather than love.

phases.label: Unrequited pursuit
phases.note: She angles for Darcy and is jealous of his interest in Elizabeth.

phases.label: Close friends
phases.note: Bingley relies on Darcy’s judgement.

phases.label: Close friends
phases.note: Darcy admits persuading Bingley that Jane was indifferent to him.

phases.label: Strained
phases.note: Elizabeth is dismayed by Charlotte’s engagement to Collins.

phases.label: Friends
phases.note: Jane is invited to dine at Netherfield.

phases.label: Cooled
phases.note: Caroline’s coldness in London shows Jane the friendship was hollow.

phases.label: Estranged
phases.note: They meet in Meryton; both change colour.

phases.label: Bitter enemies
phases.note: Wickham, son of the late Mr. Darcy’s steward, claims Darcy denied him a promised living.

phases.label: Bitter enemies
phases.note: Darcy’s letter: Wickham took £3,000 in lieu of the living, squandered it, and tried to elope with Georgiana.

phases.label: Paid off
phases.note: Darcy pays Wickham’s debts to secure his marriage to Lydia.

phases.label: Attempted elopement
phases.note: At Ramsgate he persuaded her to agree to elope; Darcy discovered it in time.

phases.label: Rector & patroness
phases.note: Collins holds the living at Hunsford by her favour, and flatters her endlessly.

phases.label: Guest at Rosings
phases.note: Elizabeth is unintimidated by her questioning.

phases.label: Confrontation
phases.note: Lady Catherine demands a promise never to accept Darcy; Elizabeth refuses.

phases.label: Housekeeper
phases.note: Has known him since he was four and praises his goodness.

phases.label: Introduced at Pemberley
phases.note: Darcy invites him to fish in his stream.

phases.label: Secret arrangement
phases.note: Darcy insists on settling Lydia’s marriage himself and lets Gardiner take the credit.

provenance.method: Hand-curated from the public-domain text, with section numbers following the edition named in `edition`. Drafted with AI assistance; awaiting a line-by-line human review.

review.notes: Spot-check chapter/scene numbers against the stated edition before marking as reviewed.
